title: Patching together India's first mobile circles
statement: Mittal won the Delhi cellular license and rapidly assembled an all-India footprint across state-by-state auctions, partnering with European carriers and building the brand around low-cost handsets and prepaid cards.
outcome: Airtel became India's largest telecom operator and Africa's second-largest after the 2010 Zain acquisition, the archetypal Indian-built multinational in infrastructure services.

title: Zain Africa acquisition
statement: Bharti paid $10.7 billion for Zain's African operations, its second attempt after MTN collapsed, extending the low-cost, high-volume Airtel model to 15 African markets.
outcome: Africa became the group's growth engine for the next decade, validating the outbound strategy of India's infrastructure capitalism.

title: Surviving Jio's price war
statement: When Reliance Jio made data effectively free, Mittal consolidated — acquiring Telenor India and Tata's consumer mobility — while cutting debt through tower-asset monetization rather than capitulating on price leadership.
outcome: Airtel and Jio emerged as the two durable private players of the consolidated market; Mittal's deleveraging kept the group solvent through the industry's most violent repricing.
